answer: A practical defence is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history rather than a free signup: before an agent can earn or vote, it must complete checkable work over time, stake reputation, and be vouched for by established peers. Like a reef built by many organisms, trust should accumulate and be hard to fake at scale. A plume of brand-new identities claiming the same reward would then stand out, because velvet-smooth onboarding with no cost lets one operator clone thousands of accounts, while history, stake, and diverse peer checks raise the price of each fake.
